4
An aircraft travels along a horizontal path. Two of the forces that act horizontally on the aircraft
are the thrust force of the engines and the force due to the wind. The vector diagram for these
forces is shown.
force due
to the wind
thrust force
of the engines
Which vector represents the resultant horizontal force acting on the aircraft due to these two
forces?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the two given vectors start tail-to-tail: thrust force of the engines points directly left and the force due to the wind points up and to the right.
Compare lengths and directions: the leftward thrust is longer than the wind vector, so the horizontal sum must still be leftward while the vertical sum must be upward.
Think of joining the vectors head-to-tail to find the resultant from the start of the first vector to the end of the second vector.
walkthrough: Identify the two vectors in the diagram: one long vector due to thrust pointing to the left, and one shorter vector due to the wind pointing up and to the right.
Recall the head-to-tail rule for vector addition: place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first, then the resultant $R$ goes from the tail of the first to the head of the second.
Resolve horizontally: thrust gives a large negative $x$-component and wind gives a small positive $x$-component, so the sum $R_x$ remains negative and points left.
Resolve vertically: thrust has zero $y$-component and wind has a positive $y$-component, so the sum $R_y$ points up.
Combine these: the resultant must point left and slightly up, with magnitude smaller than the thrust alone because of partial cancellation.

A.explanation: Points to the right and upwards, which would require a large rightward component that neither the leftward thrust nor the small rightward part of the wind can give.

B.explanation: Points to the left and downwards, but the wind force has an upward component so the resultant cannot point below the horizontal.

C.explanation: Points to the left and upwards, matching a large leftward thrust partly cancelled by a small rightward wind component plus a net upward wind component.

D.explanation: Points to the right and downwards, which is opposite in both horizontal and vertical sense to the expected vector sum.
